cause.proximate_text: The HEPA filters failed because Engineering did not ensure maintenance was scheduled and executed prior to exceeding the TS limit.

nodes.display_name: Maintenance not scheduled/executed prior to exceeding TS limit
nodes.description: Engineering did not ensure HEPA filter replacement maintenance was scheduled and executed before bypass leakage exceeded TS acceptance criteria, despite a 2020 test showing leakage trending close to the limit.

nodes.display_name: Issue Report not flagged as system health issue
nodes.description: The issue report documenting the degraded HEPA filter bank leakage was not flagged as a system health issue, and subsequent reviews did not identify the challenge to the TS limit.

nodes.display_name: HEPA filter bank bypass leakage degraded over time
nodes.description: Upstream and downstream HEPA filter bank bypass leakage increased from 0.044%/0.046% (2020 test) to 0.11%/0.16% (2025 test), exceeding the TS acceptance criteria.

nodes.display_name: Overlapping dual-train inoperability not entered into action tracking
nodes.description: Because the exact date the B train became inoperable could not be determined, there were times both A and B SGTS trains were inoperable concurrently, and the required action for that condition was not entered.

nodes.display_name: B train SGTS HEPA filter bypass leakage exceeded TS limit
nodes.duration: unknown (indeterminate onset); declared operable after ~27h04m from test start

nodes.display_name: Replace HEPA filters on B train SGTS and retest
Review open deficiencies on TS equipment for proper scheduling
Add post-test trending analysis task to Charcoal/HEPA surveillance work packages

chain: Engineering failed to schedule/execute maintenance despite trending leakage [cause TBD] -> HEPA filter bypass leakage degraded (0.044/0.046% -> 0.11/0.16%) & Issue Report not flagged as system health issue -> B train SGTS HEPA leakage exceeds TS limit -> overlapping dual-train (A&B) inoperability not entered into action tracking
notes: Cause code is TBD/provisional per FORM-366 fields; category kept as 'provisional' verbatim. No component identifier or manufacturer given in Component Data section. No BACKED_UP_BY edges emitted: narrative states the B train filter train remained available to perform its design basis function despite the exceedance, but this describes the same train's continued function, not a distinct backup system providing coverage during inoperability -- and the A train is itself flagged as inoperable during overlapping periods, so it cannot be modeled as an operable backup. No previous similar occurrences reported (narrative explicitly states none in past ten years), so no stub LER/SIMILAR_TO edge emitted.
